key_insight: Heat loss to the channel walls strongly alters early flame propagation, helping trigger tulip flame formation and its later distortion in confined hydrogen-air channels.
engineering_relevance: Accurately accounting for wall heat transfer is critical for predicting flame stability and pressure-risk behavior in narrow combustors, ducts, and safety-critical combustion systems.
method: Direct numerical simulation of the fully compressible reactive Navier–Stokes equations.
Detailed chemical kinetics and transport for stoichiometric hydrogen-air combustion.
Coupled conductive heat transfer in the channel walls with convective and radiative boundary losses at the outer wall.
evidence_signal: The simulations were compared against adiabatic-wall cases and reproduced the main experimentally observed features of flame dynamics, including tulip and distorted tulip flame formation.
watch_item: Results may depend on the assumed wall heat-transfer model, material properties, and 2D/cylindrical confinement, so extrapolation to other geometries or fuels should be cautious.
paper_title: The Effect of Heat Loss During the Early Stages of Flame Propagation and Tulip Flame Formation
